land.text: Messana and its peninsula, a Roman ally from 264

successors.note: The row's end (257) is Cliopatria's; Messana remained an allied city inside Roman Sicily.

correction.text: the -271 shape (Messana and the north-eastern tip of Sicily) from the seizure of the city in 288 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Campanian mercenaries 'claimed Messina for themselves in 288 BC' after killing most residents; Cliopatria starts the row only in 271. Seventeen years are added with the same 934 km2 shape.

933.8 km2, bbox 15.08-15.63 E, 37.90-38.29 N: Messana and its peninsula to the Peloritani. Right as drawn, though 'In around 270 BC' Hiero II 'easily defeated them' at the Longanus 'on the plain of Mylae' and 'proclaimed himself king'; the pages give no land change, so the shape stands. The verdict is 'adjust' only because the keyframe's end is restated (265) and the series now begins in 288.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, under Roman protection

keyframe_review.note: Identical 933.8 km2 shape, 264-257. The Mamertines 'appealed to Rome to be allowed into the protection of the Roman people' and Rome 'responded by entering into an alliance with the Mamertines': from 264 the land is a Roman ally's (tint from the roman-republic dossier, vassal_start mamertines 264). Cliopatria's end in 257 has no event on the page ('the Mamertines were lost to the historical record'); kept at confidence 1.

region.text: Messana and the north-eastern tip of Sicily

ledger.note: 288 BC: Messana seized. The 'Greek mercenaries' of 'Italic' origin hired from Campania by Agathocles (361-289) 'betrayed their hosts and killed most residents' and 'claimed Messina for themselves in 288 BC', taking the name Mamertines. The city was a Greek colony (Zancle/Messana) until then.

region.text: the Mylae plain and the Mamertine hinterland

ledger.note: c. 270 BC: war with Syracuse. 'In around 270 BC' Syracuse 'noticed their exploits'; Hiero II met them 'at the Longanus River on the plain of Mylae' and 'easily defeated them and proclaimed himself king' (the page gives no year for the battle; the Hiero page has him king from 270). The Mamertine raiding country west of Messana is the zone.

region.text: the harbour and citadel of Messana

ledger.note: 265 BC: a Carthaginian garrison. 'When Hiero returned to besiege Messina in 265 BC, the Mamertines called on a Carthaginian fleet, which occupied the harbour of Messina.' Hatched for Carthage on the harbour and citadel.
264 BC: the Carthaginian garrison leaves as the Romans cross; the First Punic War opens at Messana (First Punic War page: the war began in 264 over Messana).
264 BC: Hiero's siege is raised when the Roman army lands; 'the Syracusan/Mamertine conflict escalated into the First Punic War'. Hiero made peace with Rome in 263 (roman-republic dossier).

257 BC: the row ends. 'Once the larger Punic Wars overtook them, the Mamertines were lost to the historical record'; the page gives no date for the end of the Mamertine state and Rome's ally Messana lived on as a city (the 'Mamertine wine' 'was still known and enjoyed in the 1st century'). Cliopatria's 257 is kept at confidence 1; the land passes to the Roman ally tint and, with Sicily, to the Republic (the First Punic War page: Sicily Roman from 241).

wars.name: Mamertine-Syracusan war
wars.outcome: Hiero's victory at the Longanus (c. 270) and siege of 265 undone by the Carthaginian garrison and the Roman landing of 264; the conflict 'escalated into the First Punic War'

certainty.note: A single city's territory; the inland edge toward the Peloritani is Cliopatria's guess.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Mamertines' row (-271..-257, two identical 933.8 km2 shapes) is carried back to 288, when the Campanian mercenaries 'claimed Messina for themselves in 288 BC' (new keyframe mamertines_-288). The two drawn shapes are right as land; the second (264-257) is the same land under Roman protection, tinted from the roman-republic dossier (vassal_start 264, vassal_end 257). The Carthaginian harbour garrison of 265-264 is hatched as an occupation of the harbour only. Hiero's victory 'around 270' at the Longanus and the siege of 265 are contests, not land changes. The end year 257 has no event on any page opened; it is kept at confidence 1 because the Mamertines 'were lost to the historical record' and the city's land is Roman-allied Sicily in any case. Counterparts: greek-city-states (Messana was Greek before 288), syracuse (new dossier), carthage, roman-republic.
